entries.title: Stable Seat Reconnecting
entries.entry_condition: A local or approved remote human controller disconnects from an existing stable seat and reconnect grace behavior begins.
entries.exit_condition: The same controller reconnects to the reserved seat or deterministic game control activates at a safe handoff after the configured grace rule.
entries.purpose: Show that the same stable seat remains reserved and unchanged while reconnecting, without implying defeat, removal, replacement, reset, or immediate surrogate action.
visual_guidance: Retain the same seat tile, public character or form, location, condition, and item count while changing only the control-source state.
Use a text label and neutral reconnect icon rather than color or alarm animation alone.
Keep the board and current decision visible unless the current action is privately shielded.
negative_constraints: No defeat, eliminated, left the Tale, character lost, respawn, or replacement language.
No irreversible surrogate decision immediately after a brief controller interruption.
No public narration of private state acquired by the disconnected seat.
human_validation_questions: Do players understand that the seat and character remain present while only the controller is reconnecting?
Is grace behavior clear without creating panic, blame, or a false countdown during protected atomic actions?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no reconnect timing, controller detection, network behavior, pause rule, surrogate activation, or runtime continuity is approved.

entries.title: Stable Seat Under Game Control
entries.entry_condition: Reconnect grace has ended or an authorized departure has committed, and deterministic game control assumes the same seat at a safe handoff.
entries.exit_condition: Game control continues, the seat reaches a terminal result, or an authorized human takeover completes at another safe handoff.
entries.purpose: Confirm game control of the unchanged stable seat while keeping the seat active, eligible for ordinary play, and available for authorized takeover.
visual_guidance: Keep the same seat marker and public silhouette; change only the control-source label and neutral controller glyph.
Show active turn, vote, response, or pass ownership exactly as for a human-controlled seat.
Use no robot face, AI personality portrait, or faction-revealing strategy label.
negative_constraints: No bot character, NPC replacement, hostile AI, inactive seat, abandoned seat, or automatic pass implication.
No public strategy profile that reveals hidden allegiance, objective, role, or willingness to bargain.
No special advantage, disadvantage, free action, or delayed rule simply because game control is active.
human_validation_questions: Do players perceive game control as temporary authority over the same seat rather than a new character?
Does the seat remain socially and mechanically present without exposing the surrogate's private decision profile?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no surrogate strategy, action-selection logic, delay, takeover availability, or runtime authority behavior is approved.

entries.title: Public Takeover Seat Selection
entries.entry_condition: A joining human is authorized to request control and one or more game-controlled seats are eligible at or after a safe handoff.
entries.exit_condition: The requester backs out, the host assigns one eligible seat, or the selected seat enters takeover-pending state without revealing private information.
entries.purpose: Present only public-safe summaries for eligible seats, prevent private-seat shopping, and queue one selected seat for shielded inherited-state acknowledgement.
required_information: Public item count or critical-object marker
Private state disclosed only after assignment
No browsing of several private seats
visual_guidance: Show public-safe examples such as injured, Restless, Tidebound publicly revealed, current location, and public item count.
Keep every eligible seat tile visually equal and sorted by stable seat identity or the configured public assignment rule.
After one seat is assigned, replace selection with TAKEOVER PENDING rather than exposing another seat's details.
negative_constraints: No private faction, role, objective, hidden inventory, infection, bargain, route knowledge, or future form preview.
No opening several private summaries and choosing the most attractive seat.
No fresh character, healing, reroll, immunity, new inventory, or objective reset offered with takeover.
human_validation_questions: Can a joining player make an informed choice or accept an assignment using only public-safe seat summaries?
Does the flow prevent private-seat shopping while still making transformed, injured, or Restless seats understandable?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no eligibility algorithm, facilitator policy, remote identity, assignment rule, or runtime takeover implementation is approved.

entries.title: Inherited Private State Handoff
entries.entry_condition: One stable seat has been assigned, a safe handoff has been reached, and the public screen is under a neutral private-handoff shield.
entries.exit_condition: The assigned human acknowledges all inherited private state and authority transfer commits before the public board is restored.
entries.purpose: Reveal the selected seat's inherited private role, faction, objective, condition, inventory, knowledge, available actions, and surrogate recap only to the authorized controller.
visual_guidance: Use the neutral shared shield throughout and show inherited details only on the authorized private surface.
Separate state inherited before absence from surrogate actions taken during absence.
Conclude with a clear statement that control changes but the evolved stable seat does not reset.
negative_constraints: No private text, icon, voice, caption, transcript, reflection, or mirrored content on the public display.
No authority transfer before acknowledgement and no transfer during an exposed private projection.
No option to reject the inherited state and reroll, heal, restore inventory, or choose another private seat.
human_validation_questions: Can the assigned player understand inherited private state and surrogate history without exposing it to the room?
Is acknowledgement clearly separate from public seat selection and actual authority transfer?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no private-display technology, controller authorization, security guarantee, inherited-state UI, or runtime handoff is approved.

entries.title: Returning Player Recap
entries.entry_condition: A returning human is authorized to reclaim the same reserved stable seat and the handoff can begin without interrupting an atomic action.
entries.exit_condition: The public recap is reviewed, any new private information is acknowledged on the authorized surface, and human control resumes for the same evolved seat.
entries.purpose: Summarize public changes during absence, preserve all surrogate decisions, and route new private knowledge to a shielded surface before returning authority.
visual_guidance: Use before-and-now public summaries without implying rollback, rewind, or restoration.
Keep the same seat tile visible and change GAME CONTROL to TAKEOVER PENDING only after authorization.
Move private recap content behind a neutral shield before human control resumes.
negative_constraints: No rewind, undo, healing, inventory restoration, objective reset, reroll, or free-action promise.
No private information belonging to another seat in either public or private recap.
No authority transfer during ending calculation, random generation, transaction commit, snapshot restore, or private projection.
human_validation_questions: Can a returning player understand meaningful public changes without feeling that game-controlled actions were undone or hidden?
Does the flow clearly separate public recap, private recap, acknowledgement, and actual control transfer?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no recap generation, event-history retention, private delivery, control timing, or runtime return behavior is approved.

entries.title: Restless Continuation Activation
entries.entry_condition: A stable seat's prior form is defeated and one authored Restless continuation form has authoritatively committed.
entries.exit_condition: The same stable seat, selected Restless form, public continuation actions, and current authority state are acknowledged.
entries.purpose: Present Bell-Witness, Drowned Guide, or Lighthouse Guardian as active stable-seat continuation rather than death, elimination, or spectator mode.
required_information: Private objective and faction remain protected
visual_guidance: Retain the same stable seat tile and add the continuation-function motif rather than replacing the identity.
Use interrupted silhouettes, negative space, and form-specific Bellhouse, route, or lighthouse motifs.
Show active actions and intentional pass availability immediately after the public form summary.
negative_constraints: No dead player, ghost spectator, eliminated seat, waiting room, or inactive-seat presentation.
No preselected warning target, route answer, sacrifice, objective, or hidden allegiance.
No removal from action ownership, votes, ending attribution, or takeover eligibility.
human_validation_questions: Do players understand that the seat remains active and strategically meaningful after defeat?
Are Bell-Witness, Drowned Guide, and Lighthouse Guardian distinguishable without implying a hidden target or automatic sacrifice?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no defeat trigger, form assignment, action set, balance, visual asset, or runtime continuation is approved.

entries.title: Invalid Action Recovery
entries.entry_condition: An input proposes an invalid, stale, unavailable, wrong-seat, or otherwise rejected action before authoritative mutation.
entries.exit_condition: The rejection is acknowledged or times out safely, focus returns to the preserved legal alternatives, and state and RNG remain unchanged.
entries.purpose: Explain the public-safe reason for rejection, preserve the active decision and legal alternatives, and recover focus without punishment, mockery, or hidden-state leakage.
required_information: Active seat remains the decision owner
visual_guidance: Use a contained nonpunitive panel that leaves the prior decision and legal choices visible.
Refocus the previously selected legal option or first valid alternative according to deterministic rules.
Use neutral system language before any optional Underteller flavor.
negative_constraints: No buzzer, ridicule, blame, jump scare, score penalty, timer loss, or hidden consequence.
No explanation that reveals another seat's private state or a hidden future condition.
No input lock, state mutation, RNG consumption, focus reset to unrelated UI, or silent deadlock.
human_validation_questions: Can players recover from invalid input without losing track of the original decision or feeling punished?
Does the public-safe explanation remain useful without revealing hidden state or the correct future answer?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no validation code, error taxonomy, focus restoration, timing, audio, or runtime recovery behavior is approved.

entries.title: Transcript and Replay Drawer
entries.entry_condition: A player opens public transcript or replay during a state where doing so does not expose private content or interrupt an atomic action.
entries.exit_condition: The player closes the drawer and focus returns to the exact prior public decision, board position, or system overlay.
entries.purpose: Provide searchable public narrative and system history, replay governed public lines, and preserve the active decision without collecting private text into public history.
visual_guidance: Use a high-contrast reading surface distinct from decorative Tale typography and keep prior context dimly visible when safe.
Group entries by public event labels such as Stage Change, Warning, Reveal, Control Change, Decision, and Ending Result.
Return focus to the exact control that opened the drawer.
negative_constraints: No seat-private, faction-private, controlled-private, account, credential, or restricted performer content in public history.
No replay that re-executes a game action, consumes RNG, or changes authoritative state.
No loss of current decision, controller ownership, or focus when opening or closing history.
human_validation_questions: Can players find and replay an important public line without abandoning or accidentally changing the active decision?
Does the history remain readable at enlarged text scales while clearly excluding private content?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no transcript storage, search, replay engine, assistive-technology behavior, or runtime drawer is approved.

entries.title: Narrative Accessibility Settings
entries.entry_condition: A player opens narrative presentation settings from lobby, pause, transcript, or another authorized non-atomic state.
entries.exit_condition: Settings are applied as presentation state only and focus returns to the exact prior context without changing gameplay authority.
entries.purpose: Preview and configure subtitles, full closed captions, speaker labels, text scale, line spacing, caption background, position preference, plain-language presentation, music, voice, and reduced-density behavior.
visual_guidance: Use a live preview containing representative speech, non-speech caption, long localized text, and controller prompt conflicts.
Allow decorative margins to reduce before readable scale or legal controls are clipped.
Keep settings terminology direct and nonpatronizing, especially plain-language mode.
negative_constraints: No setting may alter mechanics, difficulty, RNG, privacy, authority, legal actions, or ending eligibility.
No claim of compliance, suitability, comfort, or accessibility without human testing.
No font file, final typeface, final caption speed, or final layout is approved by the preview.
human_validation_questions: Can players understand the difference between subtitles, full closed captions, and plain-language presentation?
Do enlarged text, line spacing, background, and position changes remain usable without clipping essential controls?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no settings storage, font, final range, caption engine, accessibility claim, or runtime presentation behavior is approved.

entries.title: Remote Join Request and Admission Queue
entries.entry_condition: A future authorized remote requester enters the host review queue under a policy that requires approval or an explicit invitation decision.
entries.exit_condition: The host rejects, approves public spectator access, or approves player admission without yet granting a stable seat or private information.
entries.purpose: Separate admission authority from seat authority, show compatibility and public identity, and prevent join code possession or approval from silently granting a seat.
required_information: Admission does not grant a seat
visual_guidance: Use a low-priority queue that does not obscure a critical Tale decision and may defer notifications safely.
Separate admission approval, spectator access, eligible-seat review, and later private handoff as distinct steps.
Mark Open With Approval or other higher-risk policies with text and shape rather than warning color alone.
negative_constraints: No join code, invitation, friend status, request approval, or spectator entry may grant a stable seat automatically.
No hidden role, faction, objective, private inventory, infection, bargain, or seat-private history in the admission queue.
No unrestricted open join default, silent host bypass, or notification cascade over critical gameplay.
human_validation_questions: Can the host distinguish admission approval, spectator access, eligible-seat selection, and actual authority transfer?
Does the queue remain understandable and safe without interrupting critical local play or exposing private seat data?
entries.approval_boundary: Storyboard only; no network service, account identity, invitation, admission policy, security control, spectator mode, or runtime remote flow is approved.
